note: Consolidated citation gaps from per-chapter polishing reviews. Suggestions come from domain knowledge of the causal-inference / TMLE literature (the automated arXiv/Semantic Scholar search is recency- and arXiv-biased and weak on the foundational stats/epi references a textbook cites). Several suggested keys are absent from book.bib and would need new entries.

recurring_high_priority.suggested_citation: Robins (1986), 'A new approach to causal inference in mortality studies...', Mathematical Modelling
recurring_high_priority.reason: The identification formula is introduced repeatedly with no primary source.

recurring_high_priority.suggested_citation: Robins, Hernan & Brumback (2000), 'Marginal structural models and causal inference in epidemiology', Epidemiology 11(5):550-560
recurring_high_priority.reason: MSMs are named as the IPTW estimand vehicle but the defining paper is uncited (or only plain-text in a Sources list).

recurring_high_priority.suggested_citation: van der Laan & Rubin (2006), Int J Biostat; Bang & Robins (2005), Biometrics; Robins & Rotnitzky / Scharfstein-Rotnitzky-Robins (1999) for DR
recurring_high_priority.reason: TMLE, sequential double robustness, and AIPW are presented without their primary sources.

recurring_high_priority.suggested_citation: Greenland, Robins & Pearl (1999), 'Confounding and collapsibility in causal inference', Statistical Science
recurring_high_priority.reason: Non-collapsibility is asserted repeatedly with no reference.

recurring_high_priority.suggested_citation: Suissa (2008), 'Immortal time bias in pharmacoepidemiology', Am J Epidemiol 167(4):492-499
recurring_high_priority.reason: The bias is named in cold-open narratives and callouts without a source.

recurring_high_priority.suggested_citation: Hernan & Robins (2016), 'Using big data to emulate a target trial', Am J Epidemiol 183(8):758-764
recurring_high_priority.reason: The target-trial framing anchors several chapters; hernan2016target is in book.bib but often uncited at point of use.

recurring_high_priority.suggested_citation: VanderWeele & Ding (2017), Ann Intern Med; Ding & VanderWeele (2016), Epidemiology
recurring_high_priority.reason: E-values are invoked by name but cited only in back-matter reading lists.
